title: Write merged settings atomically
description: The merged settings file is written directly to its live path before the symlink update. Because profile settings.json already points at _merged/<name>.json, any parse failure or concurrent reader can observe a truncated or partially written file.
repro: Proof-by-quote: lines 73-77 do `jq -s ... > "$MERGED/$name.json"` and then `ln -sfn "$rel_target" "$profile_dir/settings.json"`. Shell redirection truncates `$MERGED/$name.json` before jq completes. Trigger: with an existing profile symlink in place, make one input invalid or interrupt `bash scripts/compose-settings.sh java-profile-crisp`; the live target is left empty or partial until a successful rewrite.

title: Stop swallowing @extends parser failures
description: `collect_overrides` suppresses every jq failure while reading @extends, so malformed metadata silently drops parent settings instead of failing the compose step.
repro: Proof-by-quote: line 22 reads parents with `jq -r ... "$file" 2>/dev/null || true`. Trigger: put `"@extends": 1` in any override and run `bash scripts/compose-settings.sh <profile>`; the jq iterator error is discarded, parents stays empty, and the profile is merged without its intended base chain.

title: Generate profile IDs without a SIGPIPE-prone pipeline
description: Creating a new profile ID uses `tr | head` under `set -euo pipefail`. On bash, `head -c 8` closes early, `tr` receives SIGPIPE, and the command substitution fails before the profile is created.
repro: Proof-by-quote: line 76 is `PROFILE_ID="$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc ... | head -c 8)"` with `set -euo pipefail` at line 2. Concrete trigger: run `set -euo pipefail; PROFILE_ID="$(LC_ALL=C tr -dc a-f0-9 < /dev/urandom | head -c 8)"` in bash; it exits 141 instead of producing an ID.

title: Fall back when TMPDIR is unset
description: The validator assumes TMPDIR is always defined. Under `set -u`, referencing `$TMPDIR` aborts the script before it can report JSON failures cleanly.
repro: Proof-by-quote: lines 30, 32, and 36 write to `$TMPDIR/validate-json.err.$$` without a default. Concrete trigger: `env -u TMPDIR bash scripts/validate-json.sh` fails with `TMPDIR: unbound variable` before validation completes.

title: Propagate Code launch failures
description: The script reports success even when `code --profile ... --new-window` fails, so callers cannot tell that a profile never opened.
repro: Proof-by-quote: line 196 is `code --profile "$p" --new-window || true`, followed by line 199 `echo "All profiles opened..."`. Trigger: any non-zero code launch result for one profile is discarded and the script still exits successfully after printing the success banner.

title: Capture compatibility status without tripping errexit
description: The main loop stores `check_compatibility` in a command substitution even though that helper returns 1 for incompatible extensions and 2 for unknown ones. With `set -e`, the script exits on the first non-compatible extension instead of continuing and reporting it.
repro: Proof-by-quote: lines 171-177 return 1 for incompatible, lines 142-145 and 150-153 return 2 for unknown, and line 231 does `compat_info=$(check_compatibility "$ext_id")`. Under bash set -e, a failing command substitution aborts the script before line 232 can read the status. Trigger: any profile containing an incompatible or Marketplace-missing extension.

title: Scope installed-extension checks to the requested profile
description: Installed-extension detection ignores the profile being audited and queries the default or global extension list instead. That misreports extensions as installed for profiles that do not actually have them.
repro: Proof-by-quote: line 185 checks `code --list-extensions` with no `--profile` argument, even though the script is operating on `profiles/<name>/extensions.json`. Trigger: install an extension only in profile A, then run this script for profile B; the presence check still reports it installed because it is not profile-scoped.

title: Use a supported CLI to read installed versions
description: Installed-version lookup calls a VS Code CLI flag that is not documented for code. With stderr suppressed and `|| echo "unknown"`, every failure is silently downgraded to unknown.
repro: Proof-by-quote: line 191 runs `code --show-extension "$ext_id" ... || echo "unknown"`. The official VS Code CLI docs list install, uninstall, list, show-versions, and update extension commands, but no `--show-extension`. Trigger: any installed extension on a stock VS Code CLI; version lookup falls back to unknown.

title: Return non-zero for invalid flags
description: Unknown CLI options are treated as an error message followed by usage, but `usage` exits with status 0. Automation cannot distinguish misuse from a successful run.
repro: Proof-by-quote: line 60 routes unknown flags to usage, and line 41 inside `usage()` does `exit 0`. Trigger: `bash scripts/check-extension-compatibility.sh --bogus`; it prints an error and still returns success.
